description: Unique response ID generated on qualtrics for each new survey response.
Unique participant ID, following the format "p" and a random number between 1 and the number of participants.
ID unique to each university, following the format "u" and a random number between 1 and the number of participants.
"Role connecting you to the teaching of quantitative Study Design and Data Analysis (e.g., lecturer, course organiser, director of teaching)"
"How many years have you taught / organised / overseen teaching in quantitative Study Design and Data Analysis?"
"For which Discipline are you completing this questionnaire? If you teach in more than one discipline then please indicate for which discipline the answers for the current survey apply."
Participants were shown a definition of their chosen discipline and were asked whether the discipline was correct.

Participants who selected Biological Sciences were shown an additional question related to the teaching of ecology and evolution: "Does the student cohort for which you are answering this survey learn about ecology and/or evolution?".

"Do the majority of students within your discipline receive the same compulsory ("core") training in quantitative study design and analysis?" Participants were given an example and the opportunity to see more detailed instructions.

Multiple choice question. "How many years is the undergraduate degree for which you are answering this survey? Please disregard optional placement years/years abroad. For an integrated masters, please answer for the undergraduate section of the course only."

Multiple choice question. "How many credits of instruction in quantitative Study Design do students receive in core (compulsory) teaching across the entire undergraduate degree?" Participants were asked to use the following instructions as a guideline: "1 credit = approximately 10 hours of study, including independent study. A course that runs for one semester is usually 20 credits (200 hours of study time). A full year of undergraduate teaching often consists of 120 credits. 20 British (SCQF/FHEQ) credits are equivalent to 10 European (ECTS) credits. Please give your answer in British credits."
